page.overview:
Who is Phineas Nigellus Black?

Professor Phineas Nigellus Black (1847 – 1925) He married Ursula Flint and together they had five children: Sirius, Phineas, Arcturus, Belvina and Cygnus. He banned Quidditch during the 1890–1891 school year, and did not participate in resisting Ranrok's goblin rebellion as most members of the staff did. His tenure as Headmaster of Hogwarts would see him regarded as the institution's least popular Headmaster in its thousand-year history.

Following his death in 1925, his portraits were hung in the Headmaster's office to offer advice to the current Headmaster, as well as at 12 Grimmauld Place, the ancestral home of the House of Black which was used as the Order of the Phoenix headquarters. He was able to travel between both portraits, allowing him to play a contributing role during the Second Wizarding War.

Phineas Nigellus was born to the House of Black in 1847. He had three siblings; Sirius, Elladora, and Iola Black.

The siblings were raised in a household that strongly believed in the importance of blood purity, and as such Phineas carried a grudge against Muggle-borns, whom he called "Mudbloods" and considered "simple".
